conflict_topics: timing to clear an open bowl (risk of spill)
competing need for limited break time
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise, context-appropriate reasons (short break, risk of spill).
A repeatedly restates the 30-second ultimatum—moderate repetition across rounds.
C acts as a mediator/third-party reminder of safety and aisle concerns.
B makes a clear safety-based concession (3 min → 1 min) but holds firm on the minimum required time.
evaluation.final_reason: No party agreed to the other's timing or took the seat; A repeatedly threatened to sit, B insisted one minute was the minimum safe time to move the bowl, and no action (clearing or sitting) occurred by the transcript end.
position_change_notes: B conceded from an initial request of 3 minutes to 1 minute (Turn 9), showing some movement toward A.
A repeatedly refused to accept anything longer than 30 seconds throughout and retained the ultimatum (Turns 3, 5, 11, 14, 19).
A softened on one practical point in Round 8, promising to tuck the chair to avoid blocking the aisle (Turn 19).
C consistently maintained support for B's requested wait; D remained a passive claimant (no change of position).

round_scores.evidence: A claims the seat (tissue packet) and demands B move now; B refuses and asks for three minutes due to an open bowl (Turns 1–2).
A shortens acceptable wait to 30 seconds and insists; C supports B's original 3-minute request (Turns 3–4), increasing explicit opposition.
A threatens to sit now if B can't clear in 30 seconds; C warns of spill and aisle blockage if A sits—positions directly clash with risk/space concerns (Turns 5–6).
D signals intent to take the seat when free; A reasserts claim and repeats the 30-second ultimatum while B/C maintain the opposite position (Turns 7–8).
B reduces requested wait from 3 minutes to one minute (a concession), but A still wants 30 seconds; C asks A to wait (Turns 9–10).
A rejects one minute as too long and repeats threat to sit; B asserts one minute is the shortest safe time (Turns 11–12), keeping positions opposed and practically incompatible.
C repeats B's one-minute request; A repeats refusal to wait and threat to sit—no substantive change in positions (Turns 13–14).
C offers a practical mitigation (if you sit, don't block aisle); A agrees to tuck the chair (softening) but reiterates the 30-second demand—main practical incompatibility remains (Turns 15, 19).

substantive_insights: Core conflict is a tradeoff between A's limited break time (urgency) and B's safety constraint (open bowl will spill if moved too quickly).
A's strategy is repeated ultimatum and invoking a physical marker (tissue) to claim the seat; B's strategy is insisting on a safe, short delay.
C functions to reinforce safety/etiquette and to plead for patience, while D is a bystander competitor waiting for the seat.
No operative action (clearing bowl, sitting, or an accepted waiting time) occurs, so incompatibility remains practical and unresolved.
